A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Holo360D work and contain 16 readable pages, including four supplementary pages. Text, tables, figures, and supplementary material can be reliably matched despite layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset-quality measurements, reconstruction experiments, and fine-tuning ablations in Tables 1–5, with additional qualitative experiments in the supplement.

after.justification: v2 retains these original quantitative and qualitative results, including the supplementary sparse-view and single-view reconstruction experiments.

M1.justification: The acquisition, offline reconstruction, denoising, hole-filling, remeshing, and depth-generation procedures are unchanged, as are the model fine-tuning approaches.

E1.justification: Both retain the same 109,495-panorama, 75-scene Holo360D dataset, dataset comparisons, and indoor/outdoor evaluations. Supplementary sparse-view and single-view scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparators, including π3, VGGT, and FLARE in the main evaluation and DA2 and PanDA in the supplementary single-view comparison.

E3.justification: The 60/15 training/test scene split, quarter-data sampling, pose and point-map metrics, and model-specific evaluation procedures are unchanged. Supplementary Section 8 retains the same training budgets and sampling settings.

E4.justification: Both contain the same input-representation, eight-versus-ten-view, and depth-supervision ablations. Glass-region, sparse-view, single-view, and distant-region analyses are retained without changes.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 retain their numerical entries and rankings, and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 4 reports π3 indoor ATE of 0.093 before fine-tuning and 0.014 after fine-tuning in both versions.

T1.justification: Depth-construction reasoning and dataset-quality and evaluation-metric definitions are unchanged. Neither version introduces additional formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about dataset scale, continuous trajectories, aligned depth, the refinement pipeline, and improved reconstruction through fine-tuning.

C2.justification: Explanations for split-view and mesh-supervision benefits remain unchanged. Supplementary Section 10 retains the same distant-region reconstruction limitation and its attribution to insufficient supervision and reduced spatial resolution.

D1.justification: v2 adds a GitHub project-page address at the end of the abstract. Both still state that datasets and code will be made publicly available, so this establishes additional access guidance, not a confirmed release. Implementation and equipment details are unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 41 references and research-positioning arguments are retained. Changed citation back-reference page numbers reflect pagination rather than new or removed cited works.

P1.justification: v2 adds the short project-link statement and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Scientific wording, explanations, and section order otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 4 moves from page 5 to page 6, and Table 2 moves from page 6 to page 7, with surrounding figures and text reflowed. Display contents and captions remain unchanged; all four supplementary pages are visually identical.

improvement.justification: The added project-page address provides concrete resource-location guidance where v1 offered only a future-release promise. This is a limited documentation improvement; scientific evidence, reproducibility settings, and limitations remain unchanged, and the PDFs do not establish that code or data have been released.
